\section{Rules for deliverables}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/SubmissionInstructions:rules-for-deliverables}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each assignment has multiple programs. All programs should be in a single directory. Don’t nest them or make it harder to find. Remember that a human grades your work.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Programs must run from command line

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Submit all source combined into one .zip or .gz.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The .zip must unpack to a single working directory with all source files

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only submit source .cpp, .h and Makefiles are optional. Include any input files. Submit only the source files. Do not submit compiled code.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Upload through the \sphinxstylestrong{Assignment} tool

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Don’t use .rar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Don’t submit compiled files (.obj or .exe)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Don’t submit project files generated by IDE

\end{itemize}


\section{Program rules}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/SubmissionInstructions:program-rules}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Program must be complete, compile and run using the compiler and version specified for the course (the latest version of the GNU compiler). Failure to compile is a zero grade.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Program must solve problem in the assignment.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Site code used from the textbook or external source, if any.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Programs must have in\sphinxhyphen{}program documentation contained in comment block located at the start of the program. Name, AU student ID, and current date must be included. Include program name, program purpose in one sentence, and any special instructions to compile and execute the program. If it accepts or requires CLI arguments, it must be included in this in\sphinxhyphen{}program documentation.

\end{enumerate}

No matter what the program requirements, the main entry point for the program should be contained in a source file named according to the following the format:

\section{Program test plans}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/SubmissionInstructions:program-test-plans}}

\subsection{Unit 1: Points to ponder}
\label{\detokenize{AssignmentOne/main:unit-1-points-to-ponder}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Hector Barquero posted Feb 27, 2026 8:12 AM
\sphinxurl{https://learning.athabascau.ca/d2l/le/18658/discussions/threads/337601/View?ou=18658}

\sphinxAtStartPar
I’ve programmed in C, C++ a lot and reading these feels like a nice refresher.

\sphinxAtStartPar
I’ve been programming in javascript a lot lately, so I almost forget definitions of things and some of the differences feel jarring. I caught myself forgetting that C++ doesn’t do hoisting, and I forgot how strict it is with type declaration… Reading this content again has me remembering I have some javascript habbits to break.

\sphinxAtStartPar
I also appreciate that both Think C++ and The Rooks Guide especially are really short and direct. I thought at first that they were quite dated, but I guess depending where you work… the C++ standard you might be writing could be dated too. (Where I am, I think it’s an archaic standard, and the job previous to that we weren’t using the latest either)


\subsection{Unit 2: Points to ponder}
\label{\detokenize{AssignmentOne/main:unit-2-points-to-ponder}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Hector Barquero posted Feb 27, 2026 10:19 AM
\sphinxurl{https://learning.athabascau.ca/d2l/le/18658/discussions/threads/337650/View}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Completing unit 2 was interesting because it has differences to modern c++ that I needed to refresh on. I recall learning the same traditional academic declarations when first studying c++ at Fanshawe College in 2016:

\sphinxAtStartPar
//academic and traditional declaration the books seems to prefer:
int foo = 0;

\sphinxAtStartPar
but when I started working in 2018+, I used brace form since it’s modern best practice with c++:

\sphinxAtStartPar
//brace form which i think is c++ v11 and on, considered best practice to protect narrowing
int foo\{0\};

\sphinxAtStartPar
This might be another thing for me to remember since I’m used to protecting type narrowing when doing narrowing conversion, but I scanned ahead for other units and see that the text prefers explicit casting conversion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is all really good for me to read again because in javascript, everything is dynamically typed where the type belongs to the value, not the variables


\subsection{Unit 3: Points to ponder}
\label{\detokenize{AssignmentOne/main:unit-3-points-to-ponder}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Hector Barquero posted Feb 27, 2026 1:27 PM
\sphinxurl{https://learning.athabascau.ca/d2l/le/18658/discussions/threads/337734/View}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This unit was a good read. I spent a lot of time between multiple books this unit (including a javascript one I read yearly; eloquent javascript). I found there was a lot of reading that I thought I knew in the c++ books, but then it became blurry as I applied it in programming practice questions and tests\sphinxhyphen{} mainly because the casting, conversion, implicit coercion and explicit casting/conversion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
C++ prefers very deliberate programmer directed type conversion, but unlike javascript, the coercion happens less frequently.

\sphinxAtStartPar
javascript mutates the types more freely so coercion feels like something to always watch for, and programming explicit casting (conversion in js) is something normal.

\sphinxAtStartPar
I’m not sure how often I’ll need to in this course, but I’ll remember to use static\_cast\textless{}var\textgreater{} or various named casts in my c++ programs, since the last time I touched it  we used the more archaic int foo = (int)bar; … a C style cast which doesn’t seem to be used or popular in the books anymore.


\section{Readings}
\label{\detokenize{AssignmentOne/main:readings}}

\subsection{Unit 1}
\label{\detokenize{AssignmentOne/main:unit-1}}\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 1.1: What is a programming language?}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A programming language provides formal rules for expressing instructions a computer can execute.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
High\sphinxhyphen{}level languages like C++ must be translated into machine language before they can run.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 1.2: What is a program?}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A program is a sequence of instructions that performs computation, input, output, testing, and repetition.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 1.3: What is debugging?}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Debugging is the process of finding and correcting errors in a program.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Errors generally fall into compile\sphinxhyphen{}time, run\sphinxhyphen{}time, and logic categories.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Debugging requires testing assumptions rather than randomly changing code.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 1.3.1: Compile\sphinxhyphen{}time errors}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compile\sphinxhyphen{}time errors prevent the compiler from translating the source code.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
They commonly result from invalid syntax, missing punctuation, or incorrect declarations.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 1.3.2: Run\sphinxhyphen{}time errors}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Run\sphinxhyphen{}time errors occur after compilation while the program is executing.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A program might crash, stop unexpectedly, or perform an invalid operation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The compiler can’t always detect conditions that only appear during execution.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Testing different inputs helps identify when the failure occurs.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 1.3.3: Logic errors and semantics}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Logic errors produce incorrect results even though the program compiles and runs.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Semantic errors happen when valid code doesn’t express the intended meaning.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 1.3.4: Experimental debugging}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Experimental debugging uses controlled tests to confirm or reject explanations for an error.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Debug output can reveal variable values and show which statements execute.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Changing several things at once makes it harder to identify the actual cause.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ProgFund 1: Introduction to Programming}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Programming converts a problem\sphinxhyphen{}solving process into instructions a computer can follow.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Programs typically accept input, process data, and produce output.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Good programming requires planning, implementation, testing, and maintenance.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ProgFund 1.1: Systems Development Life Cycle}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The SDLC organizes software work into planning, analysis, design, implementation, testing, and maintenance.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each phase reduces uncertainty before more development effort is committed.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ProgFund 1.3: Modularization and C++ Program Layout}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Modularization divides a large problem into smaller functions with specific responsibilities.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A C++ program normally contains directives, declarations, functions, and a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{main}} function.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Smaller modules are easier to test, reuse, and understand.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Clear layout helps readers recognize the program’s structure quickly.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ProgFund 2: Program Planning \& Design}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Program planning defines the problem and solution before code is written.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ProgFund 2.1: Program Design}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Program design identifies inputs, processing steps, outputs, and required decisions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A planned solution is easier to implement and test than an improvised one.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Complex problems should be divided into manageable modules.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ProgFund 2.2: Pseudocode}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pseudocode describes program logic using structured language without strict C++ syntax.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It helps refine algorithms before implementation details become a distraction.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ProgFund 2.3: Test Data}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Test data checks whether a program handles normal, boundary, and invalid inputs correctly.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Expected results should be decided before the program is executed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
One successful test can’t prove that every possible input works.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Carefully selected cases can expose incorrect conditions and assumptions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tests should be repeated after changes to detect regressions.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 1.4: Formal and natural languages}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Natural languages tolerate ambiguity, while formal languages require precise syntax and structure.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
C++ can’t infer intended meaning when its grammatical rules aren’t followed.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 1.5: The first program}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A basic C++ program defines \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{main}} as its starting point.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cout}} writes output through the standard output stream.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Statements generally end with semicolons.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compilation and execution are separate steps.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ProgFund 5: Integrated Development Environment}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An IDE combines tools for editing, compiling, running, and debugging programs.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It simplifies development but doesn’t replace understanding the build process.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ProgFund 5.1: Integrated Development Environment}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
IDEs provide features such as syntax highlighting, project management, and error navigation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The compiler still determines whether C++ source code is valid.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Debuggers let programmers inspect execution without adding permanent output statements.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ProgFund 5.2: Standard Input and Output}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cin}} reads values from standard input and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cout}} writes values to standard output.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Stream operators indicate whether data moves into or out of a stream.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Input must match the destination variable’s expected type.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Output can combine text, values, and formatting within one statement.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ProgFund 5.3: Compiler Directives}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Preprocessor directives begin with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\#}} and are processed before compilation.

\item {}

Coercion is an automatic conversion performed by the language.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Casting explicitly requests that a value be treated as another type.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{static\_cast}} clearly expresses many ordinary compile\sphinxhyphen{}time conversions.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{RooksGuide 9.5: Automatic Types in C++11}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{auto}} asks the compiler to infer a variable’s type from its initializer.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The inferred type remains static and can’t later change like a JavaScript variable.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{auto}} can reduce repetition when the initializer already makes the type clear.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It shouldn’t hide information that readers need to understand the code.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{auto}} variable normally requires an initializer.

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Unit 4: Points to ponder}
\label{\detokenize{AssignmentTwo/main:unit-4-points-to-ponder}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Hector Barquero posted Mar 4, 2026 3:41 PM

\subsection{Unit 5: Points to ponder}
\label{\detokenize{AssignmentTwo/main:unit-5-points-to-ponder}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Hector Barquero posted Mar 4, 2026 4:18 PM
\sphinxurl{https://learning.athabascau.ca/d2l/le/18658/discussions/threads/341427/View}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This unit went further into recursion. One of the most interesting things this unit was remembering overloading.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Javascript doesn’t do this conventionally. You can write a design pattern to simulate overloading, but ultimately it’s run\sphinxhyphen{}time evaluation whereas C++ is compile time. You can overload in C++ which is really handy, and something I almost forgot.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This will let me enjoy similar js\sphinxhyphen{}like flexibility when writing functions, since multiple functions can share the same name but with different parameters.


\subsection{Unit 6: Points to ponder}
\label{\detokenize{AssignmentTwo/main:unit-6-points-to-ponder}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Hector Barquero posted Mar 21, 2026 7:13 AM
\sphinxurl{https://learning.athabascau.ca/d2l/le/18658/discussions/threads/350429/View}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This unit was a lot of reading, especially the additional and further reading. One of the most interesting parts I learned from reading it all was that loop choice encodes intent, and not capability. I’ve been selecting the wrong control flow all this time and now see that even though it expresses the same logic, maintenance and readability suffers.

\sphinxAtStartPar
I should be using bounded iteration (for) where it makes sense, not by default. Condition driven control (while), and once executed (do while) make a lot more sense for state transitions when I go back to read my code, but I must have picked up a habit of using bounded iteration primarily.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It also helps because the cognitive load of reading it is a bit worse when choosing the wrong control flow design. You can get earlier returns with the right one.


\section{Readings}
\label{\detokenize{AssignmentTwo/main:readings}}

\subsection{Unit 4}
\label{\detokenize{AssignmentTwo/main:unit-4}}\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 4.1: The modulus operator}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The modulus operator \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%}} returns the remainder from integer division.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It is useful for divisibility tests, digit extraction, and repeating numeric patterns.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 4.2: Conditional execution}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{if}} statement runs a block only when its condition evaluates to true.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Conditions usually use comparison or logical operators.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Conditional execution lets a program choose whether an action should occur.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 4.3: Alternative execution}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{if}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{else}} statement selects exactly one of two possible paths.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{else}} block runs only when the original condition is false.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 4.4: Chained conditionals}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{if}} followed by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{else if}} branches can test several mutually exclusive cases.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Conditions are checked from top to bottom until one succeeds.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The final \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{else}} can handle all remaining cases.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ordering matters when conditions overlap.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 4.5: Nested conditionals}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A nested conditional places one decision inside another.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nesting is useful when a second test only matters after the first succeeds.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Deep nesting can usually be simplified with combined conditions or early returns.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 4.6: The return statement}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{return}} statement immediately ends the current function.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A value\sphinxhyphen{}returning function uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{return}} to send a result back to its caller.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 4.7: Recursion}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Recursion occurs when a function calls itself to solve a smaller version of a problem.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every recursive function needs a base case that stops further calls.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The recursive case must move toward the base case.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Recursive solutions often mirror mathematical definitions or nested structures.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 4.8: Infinite recursion}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Infinite recursion happens when recursive calls never reach a stopping condition.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It eventually exhausts the call stack and causes the program to fail.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Common causes include missing base cases and arguments that don’t move toward termination.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 4.9: Stack diagrams for recursive functions}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A stack diagram shows each active function call and its local variables.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every recursive call receives its own separate parameters and local storage.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calls are removed from the stack in reverse order when they return.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Stack diagrams help trace how recursive results are assembled.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{RooksGuide 10: Conditionals}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Conditionals control which statements execute based on Boolean expressions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
They allow programs to react differently to different data.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Clear conditionals avoid duplicated logic and unnecessary nesting.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{RooksGuide 10.1: if, else, and else if}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{if}} handles the first condition, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{else if}} checks alternatives, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{else}} handles the remainder.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only the first matching branch in a chain executes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Braces make each branch’s scope explicit.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Conditions should be ordered from most specific to most general.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{RooksGuide 10.1.1: A small digression on expressions}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An expression combines values, variables, operators, and function calls to produce a result.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Conditional expressions are converted to Boolean values.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nonzero numeric values act as true, while zero acts as false.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{RooksGuide 10.1.2: Using else}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{else}} provides a fallback path when its matching \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{if}} condition is false.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{else}} belongs to the nearest unmatched \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{if}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Braces prevent ambiguity in nested conditions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A final \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{else}} can document that all possible cases were considered.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{RooksGuide 10.2: switch statements}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{switch}} selects a branch by comparing one expression against constant case values.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{break}} usually prevents execution from falling through into the next case.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default}} handles values that don’t match any listed case.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{switch}} is useful for discrete choices but can’t directly express arbitrary ranges.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Duplicate case values aren’t allowed.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Unit 5}
\label{\detokenize{AssignmentTwo/main:unit-5}}\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 5.1: Return values}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A function’s return value is the result supplied to its caller.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The returned expression must be compatible with the declared return type.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Return values can be stored, printed, compared, or passed into other functions.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 5.2: Program development}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Incremental development builds and tests a program in small working steps.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each step should add one limited piece of behaviour.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Frequent testing makes errors easier to locate.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Temporary output can verify intermediate values.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 5.3: Composition}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Composition uses one expression or function result as part of another operation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Small functions can be combined to solve larger problems.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 5.4: Overloading}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Function overloading allows several functions to share a name when their parameter lists differ.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The compiler selects the best matching overload from the supplied arguments.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Return type alone can’t distinguish overloads.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ambiguous calls produce compile\sphinxhyphen{}time errors.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 5.5: Boolean values}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}} type stores either \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Comparisons produce Boolean results.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Boolean values directly represent conditions instead of using numeric substitutes.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 5.6: Boolean variables}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Boolean variables store the result of a condition for later use.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Descriptive names such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isValid}} make decision logic easier to read.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
They can simplify repeated or complex expressions.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 5.7: Logical operators}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\&\&}} requires both operands to be true, while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{||}} requires at least one.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{!}} reverses a Boolean value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Logical operators use short\sphinxhyphen{}circuit evaluation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Parentheses can clarify how several conditions are grouped.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Operator precedence can affect results when logical expressions are combined.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 5.8: Bool functions}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A Boolean function returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} to describe a condition.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Predicate names usually read like questions, such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isEven}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hasAccess}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returning a comparison directly is often clearer than using an unnecessary \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{if}} statement.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Boolean functions make complex conditions reusable.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 5.9: Returning from main}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returning \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{main}} conventionally indicates successful execution.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A nonzero return value can indicate that the program ended because of an error.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 5.10: More recursion}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Recursive functions can return values that depend on smaller recursive results.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each call pauses until the next call returns.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Correct recursion requires both a valid base case and measurable progress.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Repeated work can make some recursive solutions inefficient.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 5.11: Leap of faith}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The recursive leap of faith assumes the smaller recursive call already works correctly.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The current call then only needs to combine that smaller result into the full solution.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This approach avoids tracing every recursive level while designing the function.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 5.12: One more example}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A complete recursive example combines a base case, a smaller subproblem, and a returned result.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tracing several inputs helps confirm that each call moves toward termination.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Comparing recursive and iterative versions can reveal differences in clarity and cost.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Edge cases should be tested separately from typical inputs.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Unit 6}
\label{\detokenize{AssignmentTwo/main:unit-6}}\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 6.1: Multiple assignment}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reassigning variables updates their stored values during execution.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand expression is evaluated before the destination changes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Temporary variables may be needed when swapping values.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sequential assignments aren’t simultaneous.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 6.2: Iteration}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Iteration repeatedly executes statements while a condition remains true.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Loops replace duplicated code when the same operation must occur many times.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A loop usually needs initialization, a condition, and an update.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 6.3: The while statement}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{while}} loop checks its condition before each iteration.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Its body might not execute at all when the condition starts false.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The loop body must eventually change something that affects the condition.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Missing progress can create an infinite loop.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{while}} is useful when the number of iterations isn’t known in advance.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 6.4: Tables}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A table can be generated by repeating a calculation for a sequence of input values.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Loops make the range and spacing of table entries easy to control.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Formatted output keeps columns aligned and readable.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 6.5: Two\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional tables}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nested loops generate rows and columns in a two\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional table.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The outer loop usually controls rows while the inner loop controls columns.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The total work is approximately the product of the two loop counts.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each table cell can be calculated from its row and column values.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 6.6: Encapsulation and generalization}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Encapsulation moves a repeated block of logic into a named function.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Generalization replaces fixed values with parameters.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Together they turn one specific solution into reusable code.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A generalized function should still have one clear responsibility.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 6.7: Functions}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Functions divide a program into named operations with defined inputs and outputs.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Parameters allow callers to supply data.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Return values let functions produce reusable results.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 6.8: More encapsulation}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Additional encapsulation can separate loop control from the work performed in each iteration.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Smaller functions reduce duplication and make testing more focused.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Extracting code is useful when a block has a meaningful independent purpose.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Excessive fragmentation can make simple logic harder to follow.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 6.9: Local variables}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Local variables exist only within the block or function where they’re declared.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each function call receives its own local variables.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Limiting scope prevents unrelated code from modifying temporary state.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A local variable can hide another variable with the same name in an outer scope.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Variables should be declared near their first use.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{ThinkCScpp 6.10: More generalization}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Further generalization identifies additional values or behaviours that can become parameters.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A generalized function can handle a wider range of inputs without duplicating code.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Generalization should preserve readability rather than create unnecessary abstraction.

\end{itemize}

\section{Chapter synopsis and notes}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ThinkCpp:chapter-synopsis-and-notes}}

\subsection{The way of the program}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ThinkCpp:the-way-of-the-program}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This chapter introduces what programming is and how C++ fits as a formal, compiled language. It defines programs as precise instructions, explains why errors are unavoidable, and frames debugging as a systematic, experimental activity. It contrasts formal and natural languages to set expectations about precision and walks through a minimal first program to establish structure.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Programming demands precision; computers do exactly what is written.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Debugging is a core activity, not a failure state.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compile\sphinxhyphen{}time, run\sphinxhyphen{}time, and logic errors are fundamentally different.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Effective debugging is experimental and methodical.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Formal languages eliminate ambiguity.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Variables and types}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ThinkCpp:variables-and-types}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This chapter explains how programs store and manipulate data. It covers values, variables, assignment, output, keywords, operators, and precedence rules, including how characters are treated numerically. The core idea is building complexity by composing simple expressions under strict rules.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Assignment changes state; it is not mathematical equality.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Types constrain behavior and catch errors early.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Operator precedence can silently change results.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Characters are numeric under the hood.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Expression composition is foundational.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Function}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ThinkCpp:function}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This chapter introduces functions as the primary tool for decomposition. It covers floating\sphinxhyphen{}point behavior, type conversion, math functions, defining and using functions, parameters, locality, and returning results to control data flow in multi\sphinxhyphen{}function programs.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Functions manage complexity more than they save typing.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Floating\sphinxhyphen{}point arithmetic is approximate.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Parameters and local variables are scope\sphinxhyphen{}limited.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returning values is the main data flow mechanism.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Programs are built from many small functions.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Conditionals and recursion}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ThinkCpp:conditionals-and-recursion}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This chapter focuses on control flow through conditionals and recursion. It explains selective execution, chaining and nesting, the role of \sphinxtitleref{return}, and how recursion works via the call stack, including common failure modes.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Control flow determines execution paths.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxtitleref{return} exits a function immediately.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Recursion depends on correct base cases.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Infinite recursion usually means a missing stop condition.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Stack diagrams clarify recursive execution.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Fruitful functions}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ThinkCpp:fruitful-functions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This chapter deepens the use of functions that return values. It emphasizes incremental development, composition, overloading, boolean logic, and more advanced recursion patterns that rely on trusting correct function design.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Functions with return values are easier to test and reuse.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Boolean logic underpins decision\sphinxhyphen{}making.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Overloading can reduce clarity if misused.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Correct recursion relies on trusting contracts.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Programs evolve incrementally.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Iteration}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ThinkCpp:iteration}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This chapter introduces repetition with loops. It covers multiple assignment, \sphinxtitleref{while} and \sphinxtitleref{for} loops, common looping patterns, nested iteration, and how encapsulation and generalization turn repeated logic into reusable functions.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Loops express controlled repetition.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxtitleref{while} expresses logic; \sphinxtitleref{for} expresses counting.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nested loops increase complexity quickly.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Encapsulation turns patterns into tools.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Generalization extends solutions beyond examples.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Strings and things}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ThinkCpp:strings-and-things}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This chapter treats strings as containers of characters. It covers storage, indexing, length, traversal, searching, counting, concatenation, mutability, comparison, and character classification, emphasizing safe and repeatable patterns.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Strings must be traversed carefully.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Indexing errors are common bugs.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Searching and counting follow standard patterns.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Strings are mutable in C++.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Character utilities avoid hard\sphinxhyphen{}coded logic.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Structures}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ThinkCpp:structures}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This chapter introduces \sphinxtitleref{struct} for grouping related data. It explains defining structures, accessing fields, passing them to functions, call\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}value vs call\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}reference, returning structures, and basic input handling.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Structures model related data.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Passing by reference enables efficiency and mutation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returning structures is safe and common.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Value vs reference affects behavior.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Input handling requires defensive coding.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{More structures}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ThinkCpp:more-structures}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This chapter refines structured programming by focusing on design choices. It introduces pure functions, \sphinxtitleref{const} correctness, modifiers, incremental development, and thinking in terms of reusable algorithms.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pure functions simplify reasoning.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxtitleref{const} communicates intent and safety.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Modifiers change state; pure functions do not.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Incremental development reduces risk.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Algorithms are reusable problem\sphinxhyphen{}solving ideas.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Vectors}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ThinkCpp:vectors}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This chapter introduces vectors as dynamic sequences. It covers access, copying, iteration, size management, randomness, statistics, counting, histograms, and efficient single\sphinxhyphen{}pass algorithms.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Vectors manage dynamic storage safely.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Size must always be queried, never assumed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Single\sphinxhyphen{}pass algorithms are usually preferable.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Randomness requires explicit seeding.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Histograms reveal data distribution.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Member functions}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ThinkCpp:member-functions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This chapter moves behavior closer to data by introducing member functions. It explains implicit access to instance variables, constructors, header files, and separating interface from implementation.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Behavior belongs with the data it operates on.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Member functions implicitly know their object.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Constructors enforce valid initial state.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Header files define interfaces.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Structure matters as programs grow.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Vectors of Objects}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ThinkCpp:vectors-of-objects}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This chapter combines vectors with user\sphinxhyphen{}defined types. Using cards and decks, it introduces comparison, searching, sub\sphinxhyphen{}collections, and bisection search for efficiency.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Collections of objects need comparison logic.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Equality and ordering must be explicit.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Search efficiency depends on organization.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sorted data enables faster algorithms.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Decomposition applies to data structures.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Objects of Vectors}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ThinkCpp:objects-of-vectors}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This chapter focuses on objects that contain vectors. It introduces enums, \sphinxtitleref{switch}, shuffling, sorting, dealing, and mergesort, emphasizing composition and algorithmic thinking.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Composition scales better than flat designs.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enumerations clarify state.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sorting and shuffling expose tradeoffs.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Mergesort shows divide\sphinxhyphen{}and\sphinxhyphen{}conquer.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Algorithms depend on structure, not content.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Classes and invariants}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ThinkCpp:classes-and-invariants}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This chapter formalizes classes as a safer evolution of structures. It covers private data, accessors, invariants, preconditions, and encapsulation, using complex numbers as an example.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Classes protect correctness.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Private data enforces invariants.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accessors expose intent safely.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Preconditions document assumptions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Invariants define valid states.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{File Input/Output and apmatrixes}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ThinkCpp:file-input-output-and-apmatrixes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This chapter introduces streams and file I/O. It covers parsing text and numbers, simple data structures, matrices, and validating structured data from external sources.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Files introduce persistence and failure modes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Parsing must be defensive.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Data structures often mirror file layout.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Matrices formalize 2D data.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Correctness outweighs performance in I/O.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Appendix: AP class reference}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ThinkCpp:appendix-ap-class-reference}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Provides reference material for \sphinxtitleref{apstring}, \sphinxtitleref{apvector}, and \sphinxtitleref{apmatrix}, used throughout the book to simplify learning.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
AP classes simplify learning.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
They abstract away STL complexity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Used consistently throughout the book.

\section{Chapter synopsis and notes}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:chapter-synopsis-and-notes}}

\subsection{History}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:history}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sets context for why C++ exists and what problems it was built to solve, plus the rough evolution from C to “C with classes” to modern C++. The point is to understand the tradeoffs C++ keeps: performance, control over memory, and a large language surface area.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
C++ keeps low\sphinxhyphen{}level control and high\sphinxhyphen{}level abstraction in the same language.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A lot of “weirdness” is historical baggage, not design elegance.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
You’ll see multiple ways to do the same thing because the language evolved over decades.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Variables}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:variables}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces naming values so programs can keep state. Focus is on declaration, initialization, scope basics, and how the compiler uses types to reason about what operations are allowed.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefer initializing at declaration to avoid garbage state.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Name things for meaning, not for the type.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Most beginner bugs are “wrong variable, wrong scope, wrong value”.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Literals and constants}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:literals-and-constants}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Covers literal values (numbers, chars, strings) and making values non\sphinxhyphen{}changeable using constants. The goal is to reduce accidental mutation and encode assumptions in code.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Constants make intent explicit and prevent accidental reassignment.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Literal types matter (e.g., integer vs floating literal) because conversions can change results.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use constants to replace “magic numbers”.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Assignments}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:assignments}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Explains how variables get new values using assignment, and how assignment differs from equality. Also covers compound assignment and common assignment patterns.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Assignment mutates state; equality compares state.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compound assignments (\sphinxtitleref{+=}, \sphinxtitleref{\sphinxhyphen{}=}, etc.) are shorthand but still mutation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Watch for accidental assignment in conditions in languages that allow it.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Output}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:output}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces writing to the console and basic formatting. Emphasis is on building confidence by observing program state and results.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Output is a debugging tool, not just user\sphinxhyphen{}facing UI.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Formatting matters when humans must read the results.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Separate “compute” from “print” when code starts to grow.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Input}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:input}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces reading from the user and dealing with the messiness of real input. Focus is on parsing, validation, and handling failure states.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Input is adversarial by default; validate.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Distinguish between reading tokens vs full lines.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Always handle stream failure and leftover newline issues.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Arithmetic}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:arithmetic}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Covers numeric operators and the difference between integer arithmetic and floating\sphinxhyphen{}point arithmetic. Includes precedence and common pitfalls (division, truncation).
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Integer division truncates; this is a frequent bug source.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Modulus is for integers and is useful for digit extraction and periodic behavior.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Overflow exists; don’t assume “big enough”.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Comments}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:comments}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Explains using comments to communicate intent, constraints, and non\sphinxhyphen{}obvious decisions. The goal is maintainability, not narrating every line.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Comment “why”, not “what”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Outdated comments are worse than no comments.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefer expressive code; comments are a supplement.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Data types and conversion}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:data-types-and-conversion}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Covers built\sphinxhyphen{}in types, signedness, ranges, and converting between types. Emphasis is on loss of information, implicit conversions, and when to be explicit.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Conversions can be narrowing (lose data) without being obvious.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Signed/unsigned mixing creates surprising comparisons.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Be explicit when precision or range matters.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Conditionals}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:conditionals}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces branching (\sphinxtitleref{if}, \sphinxtitleref{else if}, \sphinxtitleref{else}) and boolean logic. Focus is on writing correct conditions and avoiding deeply nested logic.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Most bugs are wrong conditions, not wrong bodies.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefer clear boolean expressions over cleverness.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Short\sphinxhyphen{}circuit logic matters for safety (guard checks).

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Strings}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:strings}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Covers strings as sequences of characters and common operations (length, indexing, concatenation, comparison). Emphasis is on boundary safety and input interaction.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Indexing is where most string bugs live (off\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}one, bounds).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Choose token input vs line input deliberately.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Comparing strings is semantic; comparing pointers is not.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Loops}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:loops}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces repetition (\sphinxtitleref{while}, \sphinxtitleref{do\sphinxhyphen{}while}, \sphinxtitleref{for}) and loop control. Focus is on invariants, termination conditions, and common iteration patterns.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Always know what makes the loop stop.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Off\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}one errors are the default failure mode.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefer \sphinxtitleref{for} when counting and \sphinxtitleref{while} when condition\sphinxhyphen{}driven.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Arrays}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:arrays}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces fixed\sphinxhyphen{}size contiguous storage and indexing. Emphasis is on bounds, lifetime, and why arrays are error\sphinxhyphen{}prone compared to safer containers.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Arrays don’t track their own size.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bounds violations can silently corrupt memory.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use safer containers when available, but understand arrays for fundamentals.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Blocks, functions, and scope}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:blocks-functions-and-scope}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Explains \sphinxtitleref{\{\}} blocks, variable lifetime, function decomposition, parameters, return values, and scope rules. Focus is on controlling visibility and reducing complexity.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Scope is a tool to prevent misuse, not a nuisance.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Functions should do one job and have clear inputs/outputs.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returning values beats global mutation for testability.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Problem solving \& troubleshooting}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:problem-solving-troubleshooting}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Gives a workflow for breaking problems down and debugging systematically: reproduce, isolate, test assumptions, and verify fixes. Focus is on process over guessing.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduce the problem until it’s obvious.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add observability (prints, assertions) to test hypotheses.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix the cause, not the symptom.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{The preprocessor}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:the-preprocessor}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces \sphinxtitleref{\#include}, \sphinxtitleref{\#define}, and conditional compilation. Emphasis is on understanding that preprocessing happens before compilation and can create hard\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}debug behavior.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Macros are text substitution, not typed functions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefer constants and inline functions over macros when possible.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Header inclusion order and guards matter.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Advanced arithmetic}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:advanced-arithmetic}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Expands into topics like numeric limits, precision, rounding, overflow behavior, and bitwise operations. The goal is to reason about correctness when numbers get tricky.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Floating\sphinxhyphen{}point equality is usually wrong; compare with tolerance when needed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bitwise ops are common in systems\sphinxhyphen{}level tasks, but easy to misuse.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Know the numeric limits of your types.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{File I/O}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:file-i-o}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces reading and writing files, stream state, and parsing structured text. Emphasis is on error handling and data validation.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Always handle “file didn’t open” and partial reads.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Parsing needs a plan: format assumptions, separators, failure modes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Keep I/O separate from computation for cleaner code.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Pointers}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:pointers}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces addresses, dereferencing, and pointer semantics. Focus is on when indirection is needed, and how misuse leads to crashes or corruption.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uninitialized and dangling pointers are catastrophic.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pointer arithmetic is powerful and dangerous.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefer references and safer abstractions unless pointers are required.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Dynamic data}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:dynamic-data}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Covers allocating data at runtime and managing lifetime. Emphasis is on ownership, leaks, and avoiding manual memory management where possible.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Leaks happen when ownership isn’t clear.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Double\sphinxhyphen{}free and use\sphinxhyphen{}after\sphinxhyphen{}free are common failure modes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefer RAII\sphinxhyphen{}style ownership patterns rather than raw \sphinxtitleref{new}/\sphinxtitleref{delete}.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Classes and abstraction}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:classes-and-abstraction}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces building types that combine data and behavior with encapsulation. Focus is on invariants, interfaces, constructors, and keeping representations private.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A class should protect its invariants by construction.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Public API should be minimal and coherent.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Encapsulation is about controlling mutation and coupling.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Separate compilation}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:separate-compilation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Explains splitting programs into multiple files, headers vs source, declarations vs definitions, and linking. Focus is on build structure and avoiding multiple\sphinxhyphen{}definition errors.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Headers declare; source files define.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Include guards (or equivalents) prevent redefinition.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Linker errors are usually “declared but not defined” or “defined twice”.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{STL}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/RooksGuide:stl}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces standard library containers, algorithms, and iterators as the idiomatic way to write safer and more expressive C++. Focus is on choosing the right container and leveraging algorithms.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefer \sphinxtitleref{std::vector}, \sphinxtitleref{std::string}, and standard algorithms by default.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Algorithms reduce bugs compared to hand\sphinxhyphen{}rolled loops.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Iterators unify containers but can be confusing without practice.

\end{itemize}

\section{Chapter synopsis and notes}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-synopsis-and-notes}}

\subsection{Chapter 1: Introduction to programming}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-1-introduction-to-programming}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces the systems development life cycle, basic C++ tooling, modularization, functions, and the normal layout of a C++ program. The chapter treats programming as a process of planning, coding, compiling, testing, and maintaining rather than only writing syntax.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A program should be divided into manageable modules instead of written as one large block.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{main}} acts as the program control function and coordinates the program’s execution.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compiler and IDE details can change, but the edit\sphinxhyphen{}build\sphinxhyphen{}run\sphinxhyphen{}debug cycle stays the same.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Chapter 2: Program planning and design}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-2-program-planning-and-design}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Explains how to understand a problem before coding it. It introduces design tools, pseudocode, test data, model checking, and code checking so that the planned solution can be verified before and after implementation.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pseudocode describes program logic without depending on exact C++ syntax.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Test data should include normal, boundary, and invalid cases.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Design errors are cheaper to fix before they become code.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Chapter 3: Data and operators}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-3-data-and-operators}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces C++ data types, identifier rules, constants, variables, assignment, arithmetic operators, and type conversion. The focus is on how values are represented, named, changed, and combined in expressions.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A variable has a type, identifier, storage location, and current value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Assignment stores a value; it does not test equality.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Conversions can change precision or range, especially between floating\sphinxhyphen{}point and integer types.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Chapter 4: Often\sphinxhyphen{}used data types}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-4-often-used-data-types}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Expands on integer, floating\sphinxhyphen{}point, and string data, along with compound assignment, lvalues, rvalues, integer division, and modulus. It connects common types to the operators that can validly be used with them.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Integer division discards the fractional portion of the result.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Modulus returns the remainder and is useful for divisibility and digit extraction.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An lvalue identifies a storage location, while an rvalue represents a value used in an expression.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Chapter 5: Integrated development environment}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-5-integrated-development-environment}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Covers the role of an IDE, common compile and runtime errors, standard input and output, and compiler directives. The chapter shows how source code moves through preprocessing, compilation, linking, and execution.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cin}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cout}} use stream extraction and insertion operators.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compiler errors should be fixed from the first reported error downward.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Directives such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\#include}} are handled before normal compilation.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Chapter 6: Program control functions}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-6-program-control-functions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces function\sphinxhyphen{}oriented program structure using pseudocode, hierarchy charts, control functions, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void}}, and source\sphinxhyphen{}code documentation. The goal is to make program flow visible and keep the top\sphinxhyphen{}level control logic simple.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A hierarchy chart shows which functions call other functions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void}} function performs work without returning a value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Readable indentation, names, and function comments reduce maintenance cost.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Chapter 7: Specific task functions}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-7-specific-task-functions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Explains how functions can be created to perform one focused task. It covers local and global storage, declarations, definitions, parameters, return values, and placing user\sphinxhyphen{}defined functions in header files.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Local variables limit accidental coupling between functions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Global variables make data widely accessible but harder to reason about.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Function interfaces should clearly define what data enters and what result leaves.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Chapter 8: Standard libraries}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-8-standard-libraries}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces C++ standard libraries and the reusable functions, types, and constants they provide. The chapter emphasizes using existing library facilities instead of rewriting common operations.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Header files expose declarations needed by the compiler.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Library documentation is part of normal programming work.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reusing tested library code is usually safer than creating an equivalent from scratch.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Chapter 9: Character data, sizeof, typedef, and sequence}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-9-character-data-sizeof-typedef-and-sequence}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Covers the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{char}} type, character codes, the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sizeof}} operator, type aliases with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{typedef}}, and the sequence or comma operator. These topics connect source\sphinxhyphen{}level syntax to storage size and expression evaluation.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A character is stored as a numeric code even when written as a quoted symbol.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sizeof}} reports how many bytes a type or object occupies.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{typedef}} creates another name for an existing type; it does not create a distinct type.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Chapter 10: Introduction to structured programming}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-10-introduction-to-structured-programming}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces structured programming through sequence, selection, and iteration. It uses pseudocode and flowcharts to model control flow and replace unstructured jumps with predictable control structures.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Most program logic can be expressed using sequence, selection, and repetition.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Flowcharts visualize decisions, loops, input, output, and function calls.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Structured control flow is easier to test and trace than arbitrary jumps.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Chapter 11: Two\sphinxhyphen{}way selection}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-11-two-way-selection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{if}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{else}}, Boolean values, relational operators, and compound statements. It focuses on choosing between two execution paths based on a true\sphinxhyphen{}or\sphinxhyphen{}false condition.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Relational operators produce Boolean results.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Braces group multiple statements into one compound statement.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Conditions should describe the decision clearly rather than rely on clever side effects.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Chapter 12: Multiway selection}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-12-multiway-selection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Expands selection using nested \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{if}} statements, logical operators, truth tables, and the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{switch}} structure. It also discusses branching statements and the limits of each selection method.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\&\&}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{||}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{!}} combine or reverse Boolean conditions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{switch}} works best when comparing one expression against discrete constant choices.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nested conditions should be ordered so the most specific or restrictive cases are handled correctly.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Chapter 13: Test\sphinxhyphen{}after loops}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-13-test-after-loops}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{do\sphinxhyphen{}while}} loop, flag\sphinxhyphen{}controlled repetition, assignment versus equality, and the pseudocode concept of repeat\sphinxhyphen{}until. A test\sphinxhyphen{}after loop always executes its body at least once.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{do\sphinxhyphen{}while}} when the action must occur before the continuation test.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A flag is a Boolean or sentinel value used to control repetition.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{=}} changes a value, while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{==}} compares two values.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Chapter 14: Test\sphinxhyphen{}before loops}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-14-test-before-loops}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces prefix and postfix increment and decrement, the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{while}} loop, counting patterns, and infinite\sphinxhyphen{}loop risks. A test\sphinxhyphen{}before loop may execute zero times when its condition starts false.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The loop body must eventually change something used by the condition.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefix and postfix forms differ when their resulting value is used inside a larger expression.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{while}} is appropriate when repetition is driven mainly by a condition rather than a fixed count.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Chapter 15: Counting loops}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-15-counting-loops}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{for}} loops, integer wraparound, formatted output, and nested loops. It shows how initialization, testing, and updating can be placed together for count\sphinxhyphen{}controlled repetition.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{for}} makes the counter lifecycle visible in one statement.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Integer types have finite ranges and can wrap when their limits are exceeded.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nested loops are useful for tables, grids, combinations, and repeated row\sphinxhyphen{}column processing.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Chapter 16: String class and unary operators}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-16-string-class-and-unary-operators}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces the C++ \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}} class and common operations such as assignment, comparison, concatenation, and length. It also distinguishes unary positive and unary negative from addition and subtraction.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}} provides a safer abstraction than manually managing character arrays.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unary negative changes the sign of the value produced by an expression, not the stored variable.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unary positive usually has no practical effect.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Chapter 17: Conditional operator and recursion}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-17-conditional-operator-and-recursion}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Covers the conditional \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{?:}} operator and compares recursive solutions with iterative ones. It explains how recursion repeatedly calls the same function until a base condition ends the process.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The conditional operator produces one of two values from a Boolean condition.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every recursive solution needs a reachable base case.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Iteration is often simpler and uses less call\sphinxhyphen{}stack space, while recursion can mirror naturally recursive problems.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Chapter 18: Introduction to arrays}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-18-introduction-to-arrays}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces arrays as fixed\sphinxhyphen{}size collections of same\sphinxhyphen{}type elements. It covers array declaration, indexing, initialization, and displaying members using loops.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Array indexing begins at zero.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Valid indexes run from zero through one less than the array size.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
C++ built\sphinxhyphen{}in arrays do not automatically protect against out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}bounds access.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Chapter 19: File I/O and array functions}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-19-file-i-o-and-array-functions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Combines file streams with arrays and functions. It covers opening files, loading array values, passing arrays to functions, and calculating statistics such as totals and averages.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Always verify that a file opened successfully before reading or writing.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Arrays passed to functions normally decay to pointers, so size information must be supplied separately.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Separate file handling from calculations to make both parts easier to test.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Chapter 20: More array functions}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-20-more-array-functions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Builds reusable array\sphinxhyphen{}processing functions for finding a specific value and sorting array members. The chapter introduces basic searching and sorting as common data\sphinxhyphen{}processing operations.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A linear search checks elements until the target is found or the array ends.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sorting changes the arrangement of data and can make later searching or reporting easier.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Search and sort functions should clearly define how failure or duplicate values are handled.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Chapter 21: More on typedef}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-21-more-on-typedef}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{typedef}} to make array\sphinxhyphen{}processing code easier to modify for different data types. The chapter distinguishes flexible code, which adapts to array size, from versatile code, which adapts to different types.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A type alias can centralize a type choice used throughout a program.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sizeof}} can help calculate a built\sphinxhyphen{}in array’s element count in the same scope.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Modern C++ generally uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{using}} aliases instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{typedef}} for new code.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Chapter 22: Pointers}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-22-pointers}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces memory addresses, the address operator, references, pointer variables, and the indirection operator. It connects pointers to parameter passing, arrays, and direct access to stored objects.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\&value}} obtains an object’s address, while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*pointer}} accesses the pointed\sphinxhyphen{}to object.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pass\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}reference lets a function modify the caller’s original object.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uninitialized, null, and dangling pointers must not be dereferenced.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Chapter 23: More arrays and compiler directives}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-23-more-arrays-and-compiler-directives}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Introduces multidimensional arrays and conditional compilation. It shows how arrays can represent rows and columns and how preprocessor conditions can include or exclude source code.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A two\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional array is commonly processed with nested loops.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dimensions and index order must remain consistent across declarations and function parameters.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Conditional compilation is useful for platform differences and optional debugging code, but can make builds harder to reason about.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Chapter 24: OOP and high\sphinxhyphen{}performance computing}
\label{\detokenize{Reading/ProgrammingFundamentals:chapter-24-oop-and-high-performance-computing}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Provides a transition from modular structured programming to object\sphinxhyphen{}oriented programming, where data and related functions are encapsulated together. It also introduces high\sphinxhyphen{}performance computing, parallel work, sequential limits, multiple processors, and FLOPS as a performance measure.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
C++ supports both procedural and object\sphinxhyphen{}oriented program design.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Parallel processing helps only when a task can be divided into independent or coordinated parts.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
More processors do not guarantee proportional speedup because some work remains sequential or requires coordination.

\end{itemize}
